latestPosts.caption:
You know exactly how Mrs Jones likes her house cleaned.

You know Janet never works Thursdays.

You know which customer needs an invoice.

You know who has a dog.

You know where every key is.

Brilliant.

Except there’s one fairly major problem.

The entire operational manual for your business is currently stored between your ears.

Start getting it out of your head and into systems.

Future you will be very grateful!

Can we stop saying:

“No one wants to work anymore.”

Some people absolutely don’t. But there are still plenty of good people looking for good jobs!

The bigger questions are:

Is the advert appealing?
Is the pay competitive?
Do you reply quickly?
Is the application process easy?
Does the job sound organised?

And when they join, do they get a proper welcome and training?

Recruitment is difficult.

But writing “cleaner wanted, must be reliable, inbox me” and hoping for the best, probably isn’t a recruitment strategy you can rely on!

Could you answer these without opening your accounting software?

How much did you turn over last month?
What was your wage percentage?
What is your average hourly selling rate?
How many cleaning hours did you sell?
What gross profit did those hours generate?

If not, don’t beat yourself up.

But DO start learning them.

You cannot confidently grow a business you’re financially guessing your way through.

Sometimes you do NOT need more customers.

You need better pricing.
Better enquiry handling.
Better retention.
Better systems.
Or a recruitment process that means you can actually service the customers you already have.

“Get more leads” is not automatically the answer to every business problem.

Occasionally more leads just create a bigger mess!

This is a question I ask business owners a lot:

What are you actually trying to build?

A well-paid job for yourself?

A small team that gives you flexibility?

A £500k business?

Something you could eventually sell?

A business that runs mostly without you?

There isn’t a right answer.

But there is a problem if you’ve never actually decided.

Because your goal determines how you should build the business.

Sometimes you don’t need another Facebook post, podcast or YouTube video telling you what you could do.

You need someone to look at YOUR business and say:

“This is where the problem is.”

“This is what I’d fix first.”

“And this is what I wouldn’t waste my time on.”

That’s exactly what we can do in a free 30-minute coaching session.

If your cleaning business feels stuck, messy or simply harder work than it should be, send me a message.

Quick question for cleaning business owners:

If every member of your team suddenly wanted an extra £1 an hour tomorrow…

Would your current prices comfortably absorb it?

Or would your margin disappear?

Your answer tells you quite a lot about how robust your pricing really is.

Forget the gym. Cleaning business owners already have their own fitness programme:

🏃 Sprinting to cover sickness
🤸 Bending over backwards for unreasonable customers
🏋️ Carrying the entire business on their shoulders
🧘 Attempting deep breathing after the third staff WhatsApp before 8am

Unfortunately none of it appears to improve your cardiovascular health!

Maybe it’s time to build a business that doesn’t require quite so much exercise.

IF YOU DISAPPEARED TOMORROW…

Not permanently. Don’t panic! 😂

Imagine you disappeared from your cleaning business for two weeks.

No answering WhatsApps.
No sorting rotas.
No rescuing jobs.
No remembering which client likes the pink cloth for the bathroom and which one hides the spare key under a plant pot.

What would break first?

That answer tells you exactly where your next system needs to be.

“The going rate around here is £18 an hour.”

Says who?

Sandra down the road who hasn’t put her prices up since 2019?

The cleaner who doesn’t employ anyone?

The Facebook group where everyone is terrified their customers might leave if they charge another £2?

Your prices need to be based on YOUR costs, YOUR business and the profit YOU need to make.

Not what somebody else has randomly decided cleaning should cost.

There. I said it!

You can have a full diary, a team running around all day with customers coming out of your ears…and still make very little money.

Turnover looks impressive.

Profit pays your bills.

Before you chase another 20 customers, make sure the ones you’ve already got are actually making you money.

Do you know your real profit per cleaning hour?

This bank holiday weekend, I’m doing something I know many cleaning business owners find hard.

I’m switching off.

I’m away at a summer camp for grown-ups with my sister, focusing on fun, fresh air and not thinking about business for a few days.

And honestly? That matters.

Because rest is not a reward you only earn when everything is finished. If you run a business, nothing is ever finished. There is always another message, another rota issue, another client question, another invoice, another job to sort.

So if you can take a proper break this bank holiday, please do. Put the phone down for a while. Go outside. See people you love. Do something that has nothing to do with work.

And if you can’t switch off today, I get it. So many cleaning business owners don’t get bank holidays off. You’re still managing staff, clients, last-minute changes and all the little things that keep the business moving.

But maybe that’s worth paying attention to.

Because your business should not need you every single day, every single weekend, every single bank holiday.

You deserve a business that gives you income, stability and breathing space. Not just a never-ending to-do list.

Happy bank holiday everyone. I hope you get at least a little time that feels like yours and if I can help, send me a message and you'll get a link to auto book into my diary for a one to one (when I'm back of course!)
